1.why: All eight screens are static, uncluttered pages with no pop-ups, banners, animations or moving imagery.

2.why: Each screen has a large bold heading, a highlighted blue 'Next step' callout, a green status message and one dark-blue primary button, so key items stand out, though the black Logs panel competes visually.

3.why: Single-task screens make the main action easy to find, but the required secrets/codes are buried in a technical 'Logs' panel below the card, so the user must hunt for them.

4.why: The 1–5 progress bar and 'Next step' hints reduce what must be remembered, but the user still has to transfer long random strings (e.g. 'OSsxJNi0Hw6qQMsSxAjYDHNMPXihgmPt78H2HSVqJ_A') from the Logs panel into fields.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill guidance, 'remember me' checkbox or show-password toggle appears anywhere in the flow.

6.why: Nothing is pre-filled or presented for recognition — the email, secret, password and one-time code must all be typed in; only the generic 'your secure server-backed step is saved' note hints at persistence.

7.why: Sentences are short and plain ('Code checked. You can now choose a new password.'), although terms like 'approved-channel authorization secret' are jargon-heavy.

8.why: No error state is shown in any screenshot; only proactive rules (password requirements, privacy notice) are visible, so the claim cannot be observed as true.

9.why: Password constraints are listed ('At least 12 characters, uppercase, lowercase, number, symbol, and no spaces') but no worked example of what to type is given for any field.

10.why: The available options are clearly labelled ('Open simulated recovery link', 'Enter a code manually', 'One-time code', 'Save new password'), though no biometric/face login option exists.

11.why: Each screen offers only one primary action plus at most two secondary buttons (e.g. step 2 has Confirm channel, Send secret again, Start recovery again).

12.why: Every screen shows an explicit outcome message such as 'Code checked.', 'Password accepted.', 'Password changed', and 'Confirmation recorded in this simulated authenticated session.'

13.why: Each step carries a 'Next step:' instruction plus persistent 'Need a pause?', 'Need support?' and 'Get help and safety advice' links.

14.why: Recovery-from-mistake options are on nearly every screen: 'Send the authorization secret again', 'Start recovery again', 'Restart password recovery', and no timeouts are imposed.

15.why: Layout, header, 5-step progress chips, callout styling, button styling and footer help line are identical across all eight screens.
